body:
email.message_from_string.get() fails parses the special text "Subject:=?us-ascii?X?value?=", See the following example.

test.py
```
import email
import email.policy

mytext = "Subject:=?us-ascii?X?value?="
em = email.message_from_string(mytext, policy=email.policy.default)
em.get('Subject')

```

Behaviors on CPython 3.8.0,3.9.0,3.11.3: work normally

Behaviors on RustPython 0.2.0:

```

    return self.policy.header_fetch_parse(k, v)
  File "/home/xxm/.cargo/git/checkouts/rustpython-f8ef4d934ac33cd8/0284059/pylib/Lib/email/policy.py", line 162, in header_fetch_parse

  File "/home/xxm/.cargo/git/checkouts/rustpython-f8ef4d934ac33cd8/0284059/pylib/Lib/email/headerregistry.py", line 586, in __call__

    cls.parse(value, kwds)
  File "/home/xxm/.cargo/git/checkouts/rustpython-f8ef4d934ac33cd8/0284059/pylib/Lib/email/headerregistry.py", line 269, in parse
    kwds['parse_tree'] = cls.value_parser(value)
  File "/home/xxm/.cargo/git/checkouts/rustpython-f8ef4d934ac33cd8/0284059/pylib/Lib/email/_header_value_parser.py", line 1498, in get_unstructured
```

comments.body: this is a Python level error so first place I'd look is if maybe `email` is not up to date?
